  - generic "Worked heat, melting, dissolving and concentration substitutions"
  - text: Result, conclusion and limitation
  - textbox "Comparison conclusion"
  - paragraph: Advanced calculations are a teacher extension. Initially ice is at its melting point. Bath and solution temperatures are maintained; conductance and dissolution rates are chosen. No vessel heat capacity, evaporation, solution enthalpy or resolved heat/fluid flow is solved. Ice is a uniformly shrinking reference cube; 60 salt grains encode solid mass rather than measured morphology. Left geometry accounts for water and displaced ice; the right fill is schematic because solution volume is not solved. Stirrer motion illustrates a condition, not a computed vortex. The latest 60 observations remain in this browser.
